text:
elaine: Quick ask — FinReg wants an access-control evidence bundle for their SIG review. Key checklist items: where/service-account keys are stored, rotation cadence, SAML->RBAC mapping examples, session TTLs, and a proof artifact showing MFA was enforced for a hosted org user. Can we assemble a ZIP by EOD?

samir: I9ll take SAML + MFA evidence. Short summary: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; primary auth is delegated to customers' IdPs for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we expose tenant controls and default to require MFA for org admins. We record authn context and MFA decisions in audit events (authn_context, mfa=true). I9ll add a sample assertion and a screenshot of the tenant toggle. :lock:

morgan: I9ll handle service accounts and RBAC mapping. Implementation notes: service accounts use short-lived tokens (default 3600s) or mTLS client certs issued by Redwood CA in Dedicated/Private. Signing keys are KMS-backed and rotated nightly; we can revoke tokens immediately on compromise. I9ll include a short operations blurb for the questionnaire.

jordan: On session controls: console idle timeout default = 45m (customer-configurable), interactive session TTL = 1h, API access tokens = 900s with refresh_token flow allowed for long-running jobs. Cookies have SameSite=strict and secure flags. Breakglass flow = time-limited emergency creds + two-approver audit entry.

elaine: Useful. Can infra-bot export an MFA-auth audit slice? Need: 1) sample SAML assertion XML, 2) RBAC YAML export, 3) audit CSV with an MFA-true auth event, 4) screenshot of tenant MFA toggle.

samir: Working on sample SAML AttributeStatement (paste below). This shows common claims we map into RBAC.

```
<AttributeStatement>
  <Attribute Name="email"><AttributeValue>${user.email}</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name="groups"><AttributeValue>${user.groups}</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name="entitlements"><AttributeValue>redwood:deployer</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name="authnContext"><AttributeValue>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:TimeSyncToken</AttributeValue></Attribute>
</AttributeStatement>
```

morgan: RBAC YAML snippet for the questionnaire (minimal, least-privilege example):

```
roles:
  - id: data-reader
    description: read-only access to model artifacts and logs
    permissions:
      - models:read
      - logs:read
  - id: runtime-deployer
    description: can create and update deployment configs
    permissions:
      - deployments:create
      - deployments:update
service_accounts:
  - id: poc-runner-sa
    scopes: ["models:read"]
    token_ttl_seconds: 3600
    allow_pattern: "/v1/models/poc-*"
```

samir: For audit evidence, org-admins can run: 

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://console.redwood/api/v1/audit?filter=event_type:authentication.success AND mfa:true&since=72h"
```

infra-bot: audit-export queued: /exports/finreg/access_mfa_1752104321.csv (presigned link, expires in 48h)

jordan: Also capture a sample audit JSON line we can paste into the SIG: 

```
{"event":"authentication.success","user":"alice@finreg.com","mfa":true,"authn_context":"TimeSyncToken","ts":"2025-08-08T14:05:22Z"}
```

morgan: I9ll assemble the RBAC YAML, SAML metadata sample URL (https://files.redwood/saml/finreg-example-metadata.xml), the tenant toggle screenshot, and the infra-bot CSV into a ZIP and upload.

elaine: Perfect. One more piece: add one-paragraph text we can copy into the SIG/CAIQ answer about service account rotation and emergency revoke.

jordan: Suggested blurb: "Service accounts issue short-lived tokens or mTLS certs; signing keys are stored in KMS and rotated nightly. Tokens are revocable immediately via the revocation API and emergency breakglass credentials require dual-approval and are time-limited. All rotation and revocation events are logged in the audit trail."

samir: Dropping the SAML screenshot + sample assertion and log export link now.

infra-bot: upload complete: /uploads/finreg/access_evidence_bundle_1752104321.zip (presigned link active for 48h)

elaine: Thank you everyone 10. I9ll review and send to FinReg. If they ask for a deeper proof of KMS usage we can pull a KMS audit snippet as a follow-up.
